version.description: Version is the file's schema version.

task_default_eur.description: TaskDefaultEUR is a task's budget when its intake asks for none.

task_max_eur.description: TaskMaxEUR is the most a task may be given.

day_eur.description: DayEUR caps all tasks together per UTC day; 0 stops all spend.

month_eur.description: MonthEUR caps all tasks together per UTC calendar month; 0 stops all spend.

session_floor_cheap_eur.description: SessionFloorCheapEUR is the least free budget a session on the cheap rung needs to start; a card that cannot fund it asks a human to fund it. Absent: 0, no floor beyond the session's opening calls.

session_floor_frontier_eur.description: SessionFloorFrontierEUR is SessionFloorCheapEUR for a session on the frontier rung.

budget.description: Budget caps spend in EUR per task and per UTC day.

sessions.description: Sessions is how many agent sessions a task gets before it goes to a human with every finding so far (the round cap); a human may grant more.

agent_time.description: AgentTime is the agent's working time across all sessions of a task, such as 20m; waiting on checks or on a reviewer does not count. A class, process or project may set its own (Time), the most specific wins.

check_in.description: CheckIn is how long a session runs before it must check in with the supervisor, at least 10m, or 0 for no check-in. Absent: 0. A class, process or project may set its own (Time), the most specific wins.

supervisor_calls.description: SupervisorCalls is how many supervisor model calls one session may make; the next trip escalates without one.

supervisor_timeout.description: SupervisorTimeout bounds one supervisor or review model call, such as 6m.

stronger_after.description: StrongerAfter is how many returns from the same stage a task takes on its model; the next return takes the stronger rung.

steps.description: Steps caps one agent session's model turns (opencode's agent steps), at least 1: at the cap the harness asks the model to summarise and stop. Absent: DefaultSteps.

nudge_after.description: NudgeAfter is how many identical tool calls in a row (same tool, same input) earn the running session a message to change approach, at least 2. Absent: DefaultNudgeAfter.

nudges.description: Nudges is how many such messages one repetition gets; the next run of the same call trips the supervisor, at least 1. Absent: DefaultNudges.

same_call.description: SameCall is how many identical tool calls in one session, in a row or not, trip the same_call detector, at least 2 and above NudgeAfter: a repetition gets its nudges first. Absent: DefaultSameCall.

review_diff_kib.description: ReviewDiffKiB is the most diff, in KiB, one model review call reads, and the size of a part when a bigger diff reads in parts (at most ReviewParts). Size it to the review model's context window: about 257 tokens a KiB. Absent: DefaultReviewDiffKiB.

checkin_calls.description: CheckinCalls is how many model calls the check-in agent gets per card, all moments and rounds together. Absent: DefaultCheckinCalls.

checkin_share.description: CheckinShare is the most percent of the card's budget the check-in's calls may spend. Absent: DefaultCheckinShare.

checkin_tail_kib.description: CheckinTailKiB is the parent session record's tail cut into the check-in's statement. Absent: DefaultCheckinTailKiB.

checkin_handover_chars.description: CheckinHandoverChars is the check-in's handover note cap, matching the session's last-message cut. Absent: DefaultCheckinHandoverChars.

checkin_sessions.description: CheckinSessions is how many fresh sessions one confirmed finding gets before the human is asked for it. Absent: DefaultCheckinSessions.

warn_at.description: WarnAt is the percent of a card's budget, or of a session's agent time, spent when factoryd tells the running agent to wrap up and push, 1 to 99. Absent: DefaultWarnAt.

plan_warn_at.description: PlanWarnAt is WarnAt for a planner session. Absent: DefaultPlanWarnAt.

no_push_spend.description: NoPushSpend is the percent of a card's budget spent with nothing pushed at which the session supervisor is called, 1 to 99. Absent: DefaultNoPushSpend.

context_tokens.description: ContextTokens is the context size at which opencode compacts a session's conversation, MinContextTokens to ModelContext. Absent: DefaultContextTokens.

limits.description: Limits bound every task's work: sessions, agent time, supervisor calls.

classes.description: Classes are the capability classes a task can hold, by name.

session.description: Session is the program a task of the class runs: code the coding lifecycle, plan the plan loop, report a write-up. The tree's check requires it; Document.Validate does not, so a gateway reading a version written before it stays valid.

models.description: Models are the aliases the agent may call through the gateway.

tools.description: Tools are the gateway tools the class may call: a paid tool with its per-task caps, a free tool as {}.

max_requests.description: MaxRequests is how many calls of the tool a task may make.

max_eur.description: MaxEUR is how much a task may spend on the tool.

additionalProperties.description: ToolCap caps a paid tool per task; a free tool carries none.

review_model.description: ReviewModel is the alias factoryd's model review calls on the task's account.

supervisor_model.description: SupervisorModel is the alias the session and gate supervisors call on the task's account.

audit_model.description: AuditModel is the alias factoryd's security audit calls on the task's account (ruling 188).

checkin_model.description: CheckinModel is the alias the check-in agent calls on the task's account; absent reads ReviewModel (the escalation ladder's plan D).

check_in.description: CheckIn overrides limits.check_in when set; a set 0 means no check-in, distinct from leaving it unset.

time.description: Time overrides limits.agent_time and limits.check_in for tasks of this class; a process or project's Time wins over it.

additionalProperties.description: Class is a capability class a task can hold: the model aliases it may call through the gateway and its tools with per-task caps, and the aliases factoryd calls on the task's account, which the agent may not.

eur_per_credit.description: EURPerCredit is what one Firecrawl credit costs.

scrape_credits.description: ScrapeCredits is the most credits one scrape is held at.

search_credits.description: SearchCredits is the most credits one search is held at.

eur_per_second.description: EURPerSecond is the price of a second of predict_time by hardware SKU.

models.description: Models maps each usable model (owner/name) to its hardware SKU.

max_seconds.description: MaxSeconds is how many seconds of its hardware a prediction is held at, whole seconds, at least 10.

max_megapixels.description: MaxMegapixels is how many megapixels a call priced per megapixel is held at.

max_output_tokens.description: MaxOutputTokens is each model alias's output limit, the most output tokens a call asks for and is held at (Document.Limited). The tree's check requires one for every alias a class or the chat calls.

prices.description: Prices are the tool prices no provider API reports.

name.description: Name is the class's name; auto is allowed on class normal only.

outcome.description: Outcome: forbidden fails an agent's task (a pull request factoryd opened waits for a human instead), requires_approval waits for a human, auto merges without one where the merge rule allows it.

migration.description: Migration marks paths whose change needs the human's schema review.

items.description: RiskClass is a named class and what it means for the pull request.

classes.description: Classes are the risk classes, most severe first.

class.description: Class is the risk class of a matching path.

items.description: RiskRule: Paths are globs anchored at the repository root, "/" separated; "**" matches any number of whole segments, other segments match as path.Match.

rules.description: Rules map path globs to a class; a path takes the first match.

default.description: Default is the class of a path no rule matches.

large_lines.description: LargeLines: a pull request changing more lines than this, added and deleted, is class large (requires_approval: a human splits or accepts it) unless a more severe class applies; 0 is off. Class large needs no entry in classes, where it ranks just above class normal; listed, it ranks where it is listed.

risk.description: Risk classifies a pull request by the paths it changes.

monthly_eur.description: MonthlyEUR caps a calendar month (UTC), reservations and accrued cost together, in net EUR.

server_types.description: ServerTypes are the Hetzner server types a task may commission.

max_count.description: MaxCount is how many servers may run at once.

volume_max_gb.description: VolumeMaxGB is the largest volume per server: 0 for none, else at least 10.

envelope_default.description: EnvelopeDefault is the resource envelope of a project whose file sets none, and the most any project file's envelope may set.

approvers.description: Approvers are the Forgejo users who may authorize spend in the console (ruling 128): approve a resource request or a merge, promote a resource; a project file's approvers replace them for its project. Empty: nobody.

bounds.description: Bounds are how many seconds one run of an activity may take before it raises a gate_bound alert, per activity name and a default for the rest; absent keys take DefaultBounds.

supervisor.description: Supervisor holds the session supervisor's progress detectors: how many seconds without the progress each names before it trips; absent keys take DefaultDetectors (ruling 161: no_write only).

cpu.description: CPU bounds CPU requests and limits, such as 2 or 500m.

memory.description: Memory bounds memory requests and limits, such as 4Gi.

storage.description: Storage bounds the persistent volume claims' requests, such as 10Gi.

quota.description: Quota is each of the project's namespaces' ResourceQuota.

monthly_eur.description: MonthlyEUR is the fixed monthly line for standing resources.

server_types.description: ServerTypes are the server types a standing resource may have.

max_count.description: MaxCount is how many standing servers may exist at once.

standing.description: Standing bounds the project's standing resources.

project_default.description: ProjectDefault is what a project file leaves out takes, and the most its quota and standing may set; absent: DefaultProject.

link_hosts.description: LinkHosts are the hosts, their subdomains with them, that links in agent-written text factoryd posts on Forgejo may point at; the Forgejo host and the project's environment hosts always may. Any other link is defanged (hxxps://evil[.]example).

model.description: Model is the class the project agent calls (purpose operator); the compaction of its threads calls Small.

vision_model.description: VisionModel is the alias a chat turn's image look runs on (purpose vision); the member who pasted the image approved its spend.

monthly_eur.description: MonthlyEUR is the budget of the project's chat task each UTC month; absent or 0: the policy's.

confirm.description: Confirm are the tools a member must OK: a call proposes, and the member's Do it runs it. The always-confirm set is confirmed at every autonomy level, so an empty list confirms that set only.

doc_repo.description: DocRepo is the owner/name of the repository write_doc commits documents to (the project's document repository, the factory's own first); empty: the project's chat writes no documents.

parallel_turns.description: ParallelTurns bounds the project's chat turns that call the model at once, across its threads and members, which guards the chat task's month budget (roadmap 239). Absent: DefaultParallelTurns.

window.description: Window is the context window in tokens of the alias the project agent calls: a thread compacts before a turn projected past 80 percent of it (roadmap 239). The provider's own refusal of a prompt past its window is the bound that always holds. Absent: DefaultChatWindow.

chat.description: Chat is the project agent's block: its model, its monthly budget and the tools that need the member's OK. Absent: DefaultChat.

time_zone.description: TimeZone is the IANA zone of every routine's cron schedule, such as Europe/Berlin. Absent: UTC.

name.description: Name is the routine's slug, unique in its file.

title.description: Title is the filed card's title.

cron.description: Cron is five fields, minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, in the factory's time zone.

merges.description: Merges runs the routine every n merged cards of the project.

on.description: On runs the routine on an event: configuration-version or push-main.

items.description: Trigger is one entry of a routine's schedule: a cron pattern, a merge count or an event. Exactly one field is set.

schedule.description: Schedule lists the triggers, any one of which starts a run.

files.description: Files is the kind of work a run files: human, agent, pull-request or report.

brief.description: Brief is the path of the card's body in the tree, routines/<name>.md.

skill.description: Skill is the skill an agent routine's card runs.

pass.description: Pass names the pass a pull-request routine runs: template.

while_open.description: WhileOpen says what a run does while the last card is open: hold (the default) skips the run, file opens another, and fold, a pull-request routine's only, has the pass add to its open pull request.

missed.description: Missed says what a run does when its time passed while the factory was down: file-once (the default) or skip.

tell.description: Tell says whether a filing pokes the inbox: inbox (the default) or quiet. A human card pokes in any case, and a report must use inbox: its report is the poke.

items.description: Routine is recurring work the factory does on its own (roadmap 267): what a run files, when, and the rules of a run.

routines.description: Routines are the factory's routines, each a pass that runs for every project it applies to: the template pass for every project with a template.

title: factory/policy
description: Document is policy.yaml, schema version 1: budgets, limits, capability classes, prices, risk rules, the default envelope, approvers, activity bounds and the supervisor's detectors.
